findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the leaf's Approach, Scope, Testing, and Acceptance Criteria to fan the three enrichment passes (get_parent_map / get_comment_map / get_issuelinks_map in _build_snapshot) out per configured project and merge results into the shared snapshot — matching parent epic 0e68's 'incl. enrichment fidelity' child scope and AC #2 (one enrichment pass per project, both projects' enrichment data present in the merged snapshot).
evidence: Parent epic 0e68 child entry: 'Multi-project inbound fetch — _build_snapshot (fetcher.py) iterates the configured project set for the base JQL fan-out AND its three enrichment passes — get_parent_map / get_comment_map / get_issuelinks_map called once per project, results merged into the shared snapshot keyed by issue (single-project enrichment would silently drop parent/comment/issuelink data for every project but one) ... Delivers the two-project fetch criterion incl. enrichment fidelity.'

Parent epic 0e68 AC #2: 'reconciler test asserts one JQL pair AND one enrichment pass (parent/comment/issuelink maps) per configured project, both projects' enrichment data present in the merged snapshot ...'

Leaf plan Approach only says: 'call the existing jqls_for once per project in the store mapping and union the results into the snapshot' — no mention of the enrichment passes; leaf file_impact for fetcher.py reads 'fan out jqls_for per configured project and union the snapshot'.

Leaf Testing/ACs assert query-pair count, source-project recording, per-project ceiling, empty-result, and single-project regression only — none assert per-project enrichment (parent/comment/issuelink) fidelity.
Code confirms _build_snapshot currently enriches single-project: fetcher.py:428-431 calls merge_parent_map(snapshot, client.get_parent_map(project_key)) against one project_key.
No sibling child in the epic decomposition owns enrichment fan-out; it is bundled into this leaf by name.
findings.finding: The leaf omits the per-project enrichment fan-out (get_parent_map / get_comment_map / get_issuelinks_map) that the parent epic explicitly assigns to THIS child and makes part of its acceptance criterion; the leaf's fetcher.py scope, Testing, and ACs cover only the base JQL pair fan-out and source-project recording.
findings.location: Plan under review — Approach / Scope / Testing / Acceptance Criteria (fetcher.py fan-out); parent epic 0e68 child-decomposition 'Multi-project inbound fetch' and epic AC #2
scenarios: A store mapping with two projects is fetched: the base JQL fan-out ingests issues from both, but enrichment (parent/comment/issuelink maps) runs for only one project_key, silently dropping parent/comment/link data for every other project's issues in the merged snapshot — the differ then treats missing links as remote deletions.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach, state that _build_snapshot iterates the configured project set for BOTH the JQL pair AND the three enrichment passes (get_parent_map / get_comment_map / get_issuelinks_map), merging per-project results into the shared snapshot keyed by issue. Add an Acceptance Criterion and a test asserting one enrichment pass per project and both projects' parent/comment/issuelink data present in the merged snapshot, per parent AC #2.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the cross-project failure semantics: when one project's fetch fails for a non-truncation reason, does the pass abort, or does it skip that project and continue ingesting the others — and is the error surfaced (logged/raised) rather than swallowed?
evidence: 'the per-query truncation ceiling ... stays scoped per project'
Failure path AC only covers the ceiling case: 'one project exceeding the per-query ceiling raises SilentTruncationError naming that project'
ABSENCE: no statement of behavior when a project's fetch raises a transport/query error unrelated to truncation while other projects succeed
findings.finding: The plan specifies per-project handling only for the truncation ceiling (SilentTruncationError), but does not state what happens to the whole pass when one project's query fails for a non-truncation reason (transport/network error, malformed response). Fanning out to N projects multiplies the number of external failure points, yet the failure semantics across the fan-out (fail-whole-pass vs. skip-failing-project-and-continue) are undefined.
scenarios: Project A returns issues, Project B's query 500s or times out mid-pass
A misconfigured project key survives _validate_project_key but the transport rejects the query
findings.suggested_fix: Add an approach sentence and a failure-path test: a non-truncation error on one project is surfaced (raised or logged with the project named) and does not silently drop the other projects' issues; decide and document whether the pass is all-or-nothing or best-effort-per-project.
